newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS says Canada's deficit-cutting outlook limited.
newsitem.headline: DBRS says Canada's deficit-cutting outlook limited.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said in a study released on Thursday that Canada's "federal government appears to be running out of significant sources of deficit reduction beyond 1997-98."

The debt rating agency said the government will likely rely heavily on increasing tax revenues from a growing economy, and keeping program spending in check, in order to eventually balance its budget.

The agency said Canada's government faces significant challenges to balancing the budget which include: stabilised transfer payments to the provinces, deficit increases from unemployment insurance programs, transfers to elderly and aboriginal Canadians, debt service costs and vulnerability to a slowdown in the economy.

DBRS said C$13.3 billion of deficit reduction is projected over the 1995 to 1998 period. It said the reduction will come as a result of a C$6.3 billion rise in personal income tax revenues, a C$5.6 billion drop in transfer payments to the provinces and the stabilization of interest costs which could reduce the deficit by a further C$2.2 billion if interest rates remain at low levels.
